name: Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern) — Data Page
description: Aswath Damodaran's public data page at NYU Stern: annual spreadsheets on implied equity risk premiums, historical asset-class returns, industry valuation multiples, and bond-rating credit spreads, compiled from multiple data services and refreshed once a year in early January (a few items, like the implied ERP, more often).

notes: Each dataset is one .xls workbook under https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/datasets/ or https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/ (ratings.xls), linked from datacurrent.html.

Most datasets refresh once a year in the first two weeks of January; the implied ERP history is one of the items the author says he updates more frequently. histretSP.xls's HTTP Last-Modified header read 2026-08-24 at check time (mid-year revision), while histimpl.xls read 2026-01-08 (the stated January refresh).

terms.summary: Free to use; the author states he has almost no rules governing use of the data and does not require attribution, though he welcomes it.
terms.quote: I am not good at making rules and thus have very few related to the use of my data. I want the data to be widely used and to be a help, rather than a hindrance.

datasets.name: Implied equity risk premiums, United States, annual history
datasets.gives: Annual implied equity risk premium for the US market, estimated from a two-stage dividend discount / FCFE model against the current S&P 500 level, cash yield, expected earnings growth and the Treasury bond rate; the workbook also carries the year's S&P 500 index level, earnings, dividends, and smoothed growth inputs used in the calculation
notes: The author lists the implied ERP among the 'few data items... that I update more frequently' than the once-a-year January refresh, without stating an exact cadence for the extra updates — this history workbook itself was last modified 2026-01-08 at check time.
This is the annual history workbook (1960-present), not the separate current/monthly implied-ERP figure the site also publishes elsewhere.

datasets.name: Historical returns on stocks, bonds, bills, real estate & gold, United States
datasets.gives: Annual total returns for the US: S&P 500 (with dividends), US small-cap stocks, 3-month T-bill, 10-year T-bond, Baa corporate bonds, real estate, and gold, plus a cumulative $100-invested-at-1928 growth column for each series
notes: Page text states the T-bill leg now uses the average T-bill rate during the year rather than an end-of-period rate, a methodology change the author made to better reflect realized returns.
HTTP Last-Modified on the .xls read 2026-08-24 at check time, later than the January-refresh date the page states (2026-01-05) — an off-cycle revision, cause not established.

datasets.name: PE ratios by industry sector, United States
datasets.gives: Current, trailing and forward P/E, PEG, and growth-expectation figures aggregated by industry sector (100+ sectors plus a market total) across roughly 6,000 US firms, sourced from multiple commercial data services and recomputed at each refresh
notes: A cross-sectional snapshot refreshed each January (page footer read 'Last Updated in January 2026' at check time), not a time series — coverage start/end left unknown rather than guessed. Global and regional variants (Europe, Japan, emerging markets) exist as separate files on the same page but were not researched.
Not fetched or used by any series/*.json as of 2026-09-15; recorded for the roadmap only.

datasets.name: Ratings, default spreads and interest coverage ratios
datasets.gives: Interest-coverage-ratio bands mapped to a synthetic Moody's/S&P bond rating and a default spread over the risk-free rate, given separately for large non-financial firms and financial-service firms, covering all rated US companies
notes: A cross-sectional snapshot ('as of January 2026' at check time), not a time series — coverage start/end left unknown rather than guessed. The page notes spreads can be cross-checked against bondsonline.com.
Not fetched or used by any series/*.json as of 2026-09-15; recorded for the roadmap only.

notes: No S&P 500 earnings (EPS) dataset, annual or quarterly, as-reported or operating, was found anywhere on datacurrent.html or in a site search of the linked dataset pages — see the S9 report's open-question answer. This source cannot replace the discontinued S&P Global quarterly EPS workbook.

industry-pe and credit-spreads are current-snapshot workbooks (overwritten in place at each refresh, not an append-only history) — unlike implied-erp-history and historical-returns, which are cumulative annual time series.
